title: Leap Year Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Leap Year Calculator: Check Gregorian leap-year rules and find the previous and next leap years. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example…
content:
The [Leap Year Calculator](/leap-year-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Check Gregorian leap-year rules and find the previous and next leap years. Enter your gregorian year and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A leap year adds 29 February to keep the calendar aligned with Earth's orbital period. The rule is more precise than simply every four years: century years are normally common years unless divisible by 400. This tool applies the complete Gregorian rule and locates the nearest leap years, making century exceptions and February length explicit. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Leap Year Calculator

Start by entering your gregorian year. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Enter a positive Gregorian calendar year.
2. Read whether it has 365 or 366 days and whether February has 28 or 29 days.
3. Inspect the divisibility checks to understand the result, especially for years ending in 00.

## Formula

A year is a leap year if divisible by 400, or if divisible by 4 but not by 100. Otherwise it is a common year.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Leap Year Calculator](/leap-year-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 2026 is not divisible by four, so it is a common year with 365 days. The next leap year is 2028. By contrast, 2100 is divisible by 100 but not 400, so it will not be a leap year. Try the same figures in the [Leap Year Calculator](/leap-year-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Gregorian year: 2026), the [Leap Year Calculator](/leap-year-calculator) returns 2026 leap-year status: Common year — 365 days, Days in February: 28 days, Next leap year: 2028, Previous leap year: 2024, Divisibility checks: ÷4: no; ÷100: no; ÷400: no. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Age Calculator](/age-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Why century years are special

The average Gregorian year is 365.2425 days. Removing three leap days every 400 years corrects most of the excess created by a simple four-year rule. Thus 1896 and 1904 were leap years but 1900 was not; similarly, 2000 was a leap year because it is divisible by 400.

## Leap seconds are different

Leap years adjust the calendar date, while leap seconds occasionally adjust Coordinated Universal Time to keep atomic time aligned with Earth's rotation. One does not predict or determine the other. This page addresses only the calendar's extra day in February.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Do not treat every fourth year as leap when the year ends in 00.
- Use 366 days for annual calculations covering a leap year's full calendar.
- For a date range, count actual days rather than assuming every February has 29 days.

## Frequently asked questions

### Was 2000 a leap year?

Yes. Although 2000 is a century year, it is divisible by 400 and therefore remained a leap year. Try it with your own numbers in the [Leap Year Calculator](/leap-year-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Will 2100 be a leap year?

No. It is divisible by 100 but not 400, so the century exception makes it a common year. Try it with your own numbers in the [Leap Year Calculator](/leap-year-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why do we have leap years?

A tropical year is not an exact whole number of days. Leap days reduce the long-term drift between calendar dates and the seasons. Try it with your own numbers in the [Leap Year Calculator](/leap-year-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Leap Year Calculator use?

A year is a leap year if divisible by 400, or if divisible by 4 but not by 100. Otherwise it is a common year. You can see it in action in the [Leap Year Calculator](/leap-year-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
